learn.pageTitle: How to Memorize Dealer Ron Scores in Riichi Mahjong
learn.pageDescription: One of the patterns hidden in the riichi mahjong scoring table: a dealer ron is 1.5 times a non-dealer ron, but below mangan 14 cells (12 with kiriage mangan) are not exactly 1.5 times. Memorize just those cells and you do not need to memorize the whole dealer ron table.
learn.ruleTitle: Dealer scores are 1.5 times non-dealer scores
learn.ruleBody1: A [[oya|dealer]] score is 1.5 times the [[ko|non-dealer]] score for the same fu and han.
learn.ruleBody2:
From mangan up, this relationship shows directly in the table. As we saw in the lesson "<link></link>", a dealer mangan is 12000 points, 1.5 times the non-dealer mangan of 8000 points. The same goes from haneman upward.
Non-dealer scores from mangan up come in steps of 4000 points, so multiplying by 1.5 leaves no remainder, which also makes them easy to work out in your head.
learn.gapTitle: Once fu are involved, some cells are not 1.5 times
learn.gapBody1: Below [[mangan|mangan]], cells that are 1.5 times and cells that are not are mixed together. For example, at 30 fu 1 han the non-dealer [[ron|ron]] is 1000 points and the dealer ron is 1500 points, exactly 1.5 times.
learn.gapBody2: But at 30 fu 2 han, the non-dealer ron is 2000 points, while the dealer ron is 2900 points, not 3000.
learn.gapBody3:
The cause is rounding the score up to the next 100 points. Before rounding, the dealer (six times the base points) always gets exactly 1.5 times what the non-dealer (four times the base points) gets. At 30 fu 2 han, that is 1920 points for the non-dealer and 2880 points for the dealer.
But rounding is applied to the non-dealer and the dealer separately. The non-dealer's 1920 points round up to 2000 and the dealer's 2880 points round up to 2900, so the numbers in the table are 100 points off from 1.5 times.
learn.ceilNote: * The base points formula, and why the result is rounded up to the next 100 points, are covered in <link></link>
learn.memorizeTitle: Memorize the cells that are off ahead of time
learn.memorizeBody1: There is no simple rule that tells you from the non-dealer score which cells are off. We recommend memorizing those cells in advance.

learn.columnTitle: {kiriage, select, on {Without kiriage mangan, there are more cells to memorize} other {With kiriage mangan, there are fewer cells to memorize}}
learn.columnBody:
{kiriage, select, on {The table above follows the rule with kiriage mangan.

Under rules without kiriage mangan, 30 fu 4 han and 60 fu 3 han do not become mangan, and the dealer ron is 11600 points. 1.5 times the non-dealer ron of 7700 points is 11550 points, so these two cells join the cells that are off, and you memorize 14 cells.} other {The table above follows the rule without kiriage mangan.

Under the kiriage mangan rule, 30 fu 4 han (11600 points) and 60 fu 3 han (11600 points) become mangan at 12000 points.

Mangan is exactly 1.5 times the non-dealer score, so these two cells drop out of the cells that are off, and you only need to memorize 12.}}
